# Welcome to MVC .NET

The Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern is an architectural pattern that separates an application into three main logical components: the model, the view, and the controller. Each of these components is built to handle specific development aspects of an application.

## Key Components

- **Models**: Handle data logic
- **Views**: Handle display logic
- **Controllers**: Handle request flow

## Getting Started

Follow our installation guide to set up your first MVC .NET application. You'll learn how to:

1. Set up your development environment
2. Create a new MVC project
3. Understand the project structure
4. Run your first application

# Setting Up Your Development Environment

Before you can start developing with MVC .NET, you'll need to set up your development environment.

## Prerequisites

1. **.NET SDK**: Download and install the latest .NET SDK
2. **IDE**: Install Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code
3. **Git**: Version control system

# Create a new MVC project
dotnet new mvc -n MyMvcApp
cd MyMvcApp

# Run the application
dotnet run

# Market Data API

Access real-time and historical market data through our REST API endpoints.
